codeReview.summary: The verify-dispatcher script was correctly updated to support --engine=claude|opencode flag, --help output, wall-clock timing metrics with 30s target indicator, timing.json artifact persistence, and graceful error handling for missing/invalid engine binaries. The implementation properly routes Claude to SubprocessTransport-only (skipping SDK) and OpenCode to SDK-first-then-CLI. 14 new unit tests were added covering input assembly, CLI parsing, schema validation, engine availability, and timing measurement. All tests pass, typecheck is clean. The code follows existing patterns (engine registry, SubprocessTransport options) and uses performance.now() for accurate wall-clock timing. The --engine validation at the top of the script provides early, clear error messages for invalid values.

issues.description: The `engineArg` type assertion `as 'claude' | 'opencode' | undefined` trusts CLI input at parse time, but the runtime validation below (lines 118-121) only checks for truthiness + not-claude + not-opencode. If someone passes --engine=CLAUDE (uppercase), the type assertion silently narrows it, but the validation `engineArg !== 'claude'` would catch it. This works correctly but the type assertion is slightly misleading — the value could be any string until validated. Consider parsing as `string | undefined` first, then narrowing after validation.

In the auto-detect block for OpenCode (else branch at ~line 253), the SdkTransport is created with `engineName: engineArg` which could be `undefined`. This is fine because SdkTransport defaults to 'opencode', but it's slightly inconsistent with the Claude branch which explicitly passes `engineName: 'claude'`. Could pass `engineName: engineArg ?? 'opencode'` for clarity.

The engine binary availability test uses `Bun.which()` to conditionally skip assertions when the binary IS installed. On a developer machine where both claude and opencode are installed (as in this environment), the only assertion that actually runs is the `nonexistent` engine test. The test effectively becomes a single assertion test in most dev environments. Consider adding a positive-path test that verifies SubprocessTransport can be constructed with an available engine, to ensure the test always exercises meaningful logic regardless of environment.

The outer catch block (line 290) computes `dispatcherTimingMs = performance.now() - startTime`, but `startTime` is set before transport resolution (line 213). This means the timing on error includes transport setup overhead (engine resolution, server health check), not just the dispatcher invocation. The inner `invokeStart` timing is correct for the happy path. For error cases, the timing is slightly inflated — minor since it's an error path, but worth noting.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The verify-dispatcher script uses `console.log`, `console.error`, and ANSI color codes directly for output, which is appropriate for a standalone diagnostic script. However, AGENTS.md says 'Never use console.error/console.warn/console.debug in production code' — the script is not production code per se, but this exception isn't explicitly documented. Other scripts might follow this pattern incorrectly.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: scripts/verify-dispatcher.ts uses console.log/console.error throughout. AGENTS.md Coding Conventions says 'Logging: Never use console.error/console.warn/console.debug — use the Log module'. The script legitimately needs stdout output for its diagnostic purpose.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The services.yaml file already includes `verify-dispatcher: bun run scripts/verify-dispatcher.ts`, which is good. The new --engine and --help flags are not documented there, though services.yaml typically just captures the base command.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: .factory/services.yaml has `verify-dispatcher: bun run scripts/verify-dispatcher.ts`. The new flags (--engine, --help, --dry-run) are documented in the script's --help output.

summary: PASS. The verify-dispatcher script update is well-implemented and covers all expected behaviors from the feature description. The --engine flag correctly routes Claude to subprocess-only and OpenCode to SDK-first-then-CLI. Timing metrics use performance.now() for wall-clock accuracy and are persisted to timing.json. Graceful error handling covers missing binaries (via engine registry + Bun.which), invalid engine values (early validation), and SDK-for-Claude (explicit block). The --help output is comprehensive. The 14 unit tests are well-structured following TDD, though the engine availability test has limited coverage when both engines are installed locally. All issues are non-blocking.
